html:
In 1619 the Dutch East India Company (the VOC) under Jan Pieterszoon Coen seized the port of Jayakarta on Java, burned it, and built Batavia on its ruins. Batavia became the company's headquarters in Asia; it is now Jakarta.

Coen wanted a fixed base from which to control the spice trade and keep out English and local rivals. From Batavia the company ruled by force: in 1621 Coen led the conquest of the Banda Islands, killing or driving out most of their people to control nutmeg. Ships from Batavia linked the Dutch posts from Japan to the Cape.

The city was laid out with Dutch canals and filled with Chinese traders, Asian slaves and workers from across the archipelago. Tension with the Chinese ended in the massacre of 1740. Batavia remained the centre of Dutch power in what became the Dutch East Indies until Indonesian independence.
